provenance: Procedurally generated teaching models. Not captured by the scan, not OEM drawings, not specific Valmet products. Component descriptions are general engineering knowledge written for training; they are not manufacturer instructions.

PROCESS_PUMP.label: Process pump
PROCESS_PUMP.model_title: End-suction centrifugal pump with coupled motor
PROCESS_PUMP.function: Moves process liquid by adding energy with a rotating impeller; the motor drives it through a flexible coupling.

components.name: Baseplate
components.function: Common rigid frame that keeps pump and motor aligned.
failure_symptoms: soft foot / loose anchoring → misalignment and vibration

components.name: Electric motor
components.function: Drives the pump; current draw reflects hydraulic load.

components.name: Flexible coupling
components.function: Connects motor shaft to pump shaft and tolerates small misalignment.

components.name: Shaft
components.function: Transmits torque from the coupling to the impeller; carries the rotating assembly.

components.name: Bearing housing
components.function: Holds the bearings and lubricant; a common mounting point for vibration and temperature sensors.
failure_symptoms: loose sensor mounting giving poor data

components.name: Outboard bearing
components.function: Supports radial and axial load at the drive end of the bearing housing.

components.name: Inboard bearing
components.function: Supports radial load of the rotating assembly on the pump side.

components.name: Mechanical seal
components.function: Seals the rotating shaft where it leaves the pressurised casing.
failure_symptoms: visible leakage at the seal chamber

components.name: Impeller
components.function: Rotating vaned wheel that adds energy to the liquid; its condition sets the pump's head–flow curve.
failure_symptoms: fouling / build-up on vanes → lower flow for the same power

components.name: Wear ring
components.function: Small running clearance between impeller and casing that limits internal recirculation.
failure_symptoms: clearance growth → efficiency loss, lower discharge pressure

components.name: Volute casing
components.function: Collects liquid leaving the impeller and converts velocity into pressure; contains the discharge nozzle.
failure_symptoms: internal deposits or fouling narrowing the flow path
erosion / cavitation pitting near the cutwater

FOULING: Fouling or deposits in the impeller or volute
Process-side restriction (strainer or partly closed valve)

learn_topics.title: Why does fouling lower flow but raise current?

steps.text: Deposits on the impeller vanes and in the volute narrow the flow path, so the pump delivers less flow at the same speed.
The motor current is the load indicator. A combination of lower flow and higher current is a multivariate pattern — no single threshold proves fouling (DOC-PROCESS_PUMP-CORE).
Worn wear-ring clearances produce a similar efficiency loss, which is why the assistant lists it as an alternative hypothesis.
Evidence that matters: flow and pressure trend vs. the pump's own baseline and its peers, current trend, recent FOULING events, previous hydraulic work orders.
Safety gate: internal inspection requires isolation, draining and lockout/tagout under site procedures and OEM instructions (DOC-FIELD-SAFETY). This module explains *why*, not *how* to open the pump.
Rolling bearings carry the shaft. As they degrade, vibration usually rises first, then temperature.
Sensors sit on the bearing housing. Check mounting and signal quality before trusting a vibration trend (DOC-VIBRATION_SENSOR-CORE).
Misalignment and soft foot create similar vibration — compare with alignment history before blaming the bearing.
When specialist guidance is required: bearing replacement and lubrication intervals are OEM- and site-specific — escalate to a qualified technician.
The seal keeps pressurised liquid inside where the shaft exits the casing.
Typical evidence: visible leakage, local heating, recurring seal work orders. Inspect for leakage visually from a safe position first.
Seal replacement is a specialist task requiring isolation and OEM procedure.

practice_scenarios.title: Suspected pump bearing degradation (fictional training case)
practice_scenarios.brief: Training pump TP-01 shows vibration rising from 2.1 to 5.8 mm/s over 9 days and bearing temperature from 57 °C to 71 °C. Flow and pressure are stable. Last alignment check 14 months ago: within tolerance.

tasks.prompt: Select the component most consistent with this evidence.
tasks.feedback_ok: Correct — rising vibration followed by rising temperature with stable hydraulics points at the bearings.
tasks.feedback_bad: Look again: hydraulics (flow) are stable, so impeller/casing are less likely. Which components carry the shaft load?

tasks.prompt: Which evidence most strongly separates bearing wear from impeller fouling here?
options: Stable flow while vibration and temperature rise

tasks.prompt: Before trusting the vibration trend, what should be verified?
Virtual exercise: expose the bearings. Remove parts in a valid order (coupling → motor → bearing housing).
tasks.feedback_ok: Bearings exposed in the virtual model.
tasks.feedback_bad: Not in this order — the drive train has to be separated first.

tasks.prompt: What must be in place before any real work on this pump?
options: Authorisation, isolation + lockout/tagout, approved OEM/site procedure
Nothing if the pump is small

tasks.prompt: Reassemble the model (reverse order).

ELECTRIC_MOTOR.label: Electric motor
ELECTRIC_MOTOR.function: Converts electrical power into shaft rotation; its current and temperature reveal the mechanical and electrical load.

components.name: Frame and feet
components.function: Cast housing that holds the stator, carries heat to the cooling fins and bolts the motor to its base.
failure_symptoms: Cracked or loose feet (soft foot) causing vibration

components.name: Stator core
components.function: Stack of laminated steel sheets that carries the rotating magnetic field.

components.name: Stator windings
components.function: Copper coils that create the magnetic field when supplied with current.

components.name: Rotor
components.function: Squirrel-cage rotor that turns inside the stator field and drives the shaft.
failure_symptoms: Broken rotor bars giving current sidebands

components.name: Shaft
components.function: Carries the rotor and transmits torque to the driven machine.
failure_symptoms: Run-out or bend causing vibration at running speed

components.name: Drive-end bearing
components.function: Supports the shaft at the load side, where belt or coupling forces act.
failure_symptoms: Rising vibration followed by rising temperature

components.name: Non-drive-end bearing
components.function: Supports the shaft at the fan end and locates it axially.

components.name: Drive-end shield
components.function: Cover that closes the frame and holds the drive-end bearing in line.

components.name: Non-drive-end shield
components.function: Cover at the fan end that holds the non-drive-end bearing.

components.name: Cooling fan
components.function: Shaft-mounted fan that blows air over the finned frame.

components.name: Fan cover
components.function: Guard that directs fan air along the frame fins.
failure_symptoms: Dirt or debris blocking the air intake

components.name: Terminal box
components.function: Where supply cables connect to the windings.
failure_symptoms: Loose or corroded terminals causing phase imbalance

MISALIGNMENT: Shaft misalignment at the drive end
Soft foot at the frame feet

learn_topics.title: Why does a motor run hot?

steps.text: A fan-cooled motor depends on air flowing along the frame fins. A blocked cover or a broken fan reduces cooling.
The windings are where most heat is produced. Heat ages their insulation, so a sustained temperature rise shortens motor life.
Evidence that matters: temperature trend against the motor's own baseline and its peers, current draw, ambient conditions and recent cleaning work [DOC-ELECTRIC_MOTOR-CORE].
Inspecting windings or terminals requires electrical isolation and qualified personnel [DOC-FIELD-SAFETY]. This lesson explains why, not how.
Each phase should carry about the same current. Loose or corroded terminals are a common, simple cause of imbalance.
Winding damage also unbalances the phases and usually comes with extra heat.
Rotor bar faults show up as slow current fluctuation at the running speed, which needs a specialist measurement to confirm.
Prefer trend evidence over a single reading [DOC-ELECTRIC_MOTOR-CORE].

practice_scenarios.title: Drive-end bearing check on a motor (fictional training case)
practice_scenarios.brief: Training motor TM-02 shows vibration rising from 1.8 to 4.9 mm/s over 12 days and bearing temperature from 52 °C to 66 °C. Current is stable.

tasks.prompt: Select the component most consistent with this evidence.
tasks.feedback_ok: Correct. Rising vibration then temperature with steady current points at the bearings.
tasks.feedback_bad: Current is steady, so the electrical parts are less likely. What carries the shaft?

tasks.prompt: What separates a bearing fault from a winding fault here?
options: Steady current while vibration and temperature rise

tasks.prompt: What must be in place before any real work on a motor?
options: Authorisation, electrical isolation with lockout/tagout, approved procedure

tasks.prompt: Virtual exercise: reach the non-drive-end bearing. Remove parts in a valid order.
tasks.feedback_ok: Non-drive-end bearing exposed in the virtual model.
tasks.feedback_bad: Not in this order. The cover and fan sit in front of the end shield.

tasks.prompt: Reassemble the model (reverse order).

CONTROL_VALVE.label: Control valve
CONTROL_VALVE.model_title: Globe control valve with spring-diaphragm actuator and positioner
CONTROL_VALVE.function: Throttles process flow to the position the control system asks for; the positioner compares setpoint and actual stem position.

components.name: Valve body
components.function: Pressure-retaining body with the flow passage and end flanges.

components.name: Seat ring
components.function: Hardened ring the plug closes against; sets tight shut-off.
failure_symptoms: Wear or erosion causing seat leakage

components.name: Plug
components.function: Moving part that sets the flow opening; its shape defines the flow characteristic.

components.name: Stem
components.function: Connects the actuator to the plug and transmits the stroke.

components.name: Bonnet
components.function: Closes the top of the body and guides the stem.

components.name: Stem packing
components.function: Rings that seal the stem against process pressure; too tight adds friction, too loose leaks.

components.name: Yoke
components.function: Frame that holds the actuator on the bonnet and carries the position feedback linkage.

components.name: Diaphragm actuator
components.function: Air pressure on a diaphragm moves the stem against a spring; the spring returns it on air failure.
failure_symptoms: Weak spring changing the fail position

components.name: Diaphragm
components.function: Flexible membrane inside the actuator that turns air pressure into stem force.

components.name: Actuator spring
components.function: Returns the valve to its safe position when air is lost.

components.name: Positioner
components.function: Compares the control signal with the measured stem position and adjusts actuator air.

POSITION_DEVIATION: Actuator or positioner not tracking the setpoint
Friction at the packing or plug

learn_topics.title: Why does a valve miss its setpoint?

steps.text: The positioner compares where the valve should be with where the stem actually is, and adjusts the actuator air to close the gap.
If the actuator cannot deliver enough force, because of low supply air or a leaking diaphragm, the valve lags behind the setpoint.
Friction at the packing or plug makes the valve stick and then jump. This is stiction, visible as a stepped position trend.
Use position, controller diagnostics, supply pressure and history together; each signal alone is an investigation lead, not proof [DOC-CONTROL_VALVE-CORE].

practice_scenarios.title: Sticking control valve (fictional training case)
practice_scenarios.brief: Training valve TV-07 follows its setpoint in steps instead of smoothly. The stiction index has risen from 6 to 19 over two weeks; supply air is normal.

tasks.prompt: Supply air is normal. Select the component most likely to add friction.
tasks.feedback_ok: Correct. With normal air, rising stiction and opening load point at packing or plug friction.
tasks.feedback_bad: Air supply is normal, so the actuator force is fine. Where does the stem rub?

tasks.prompt: Which evidence rules out low supply air?
What must be in place before any work on a valve in service?
options: Authorisation, process isolation and depressurisation, approved procedure
Closing the valve from the control room
Nothing if the valve is small

tasks.prompt: Virtual exercise: reach the packing. Remove parts in a valid order.
tasks.feedback_ok: Packing area exposed in the virtual model.
tasks.feedback_bad: Not in this order. The positioner and actuator are mounted above the yoke.

tasks.prompt: Reassemble the model (reverse order).

PRESSURE_TRANSMITTER.label: Pressure transmitter
PRESSURE_TRANSMITTER.function: Measures process pressure through an isolating diaphragm and sends it to the control system as a signal.

components.name: Process connection
components.function: Threaded connection that brings process pressure to the sensor.
failure_symptoms: Plugged impulse line giving a frozen reading

components.name: Isolating diaphragm
components.function: Thin membrane that passes pressure to the sensor fill fluid while keeping the process out.
failure_symptoms: Coating or corrosion shifting the reading

components.name: Sensor module
components.function: Converts pressure into an electrical value; its stability sets long-term accuracy.

components.name: Housing
components.function: Two-compartment enclosure for the electronics and the field wiring.
failure_symptoms: Moisture ingress through a damaged seal

components.name: Electronics module
components.function: Linearises the sensor value and drives the output signal and diagnostics.

components.name: Display cover
components.function: Threaded window cover that seals the electronics compartment.

components.name: Terminal compartment
components.function: Where the field cable is connected; separated from the electronics.
failure_symptoms: Loose or corroded terminals causing intermittent signal

components.name: Cable gland
components.function: Seals the cable entry against dust and water.
failure_symptoms: Loose gland letting moisture reach the terminals

learn_topics.title: Is it the process or the transmitter?

steps.text: Pressure reaches the sensor through a thin diaphragm. Coating or damage there, or ageing of the sensor, shifts the reading slowly.
A plugged impulse line freezes the reading even though the process changes. Compare against a neighbouring measurement or a reference.
Signal dropouts usually come from wiring or moisture, not from the sensor itself.
Assess continuity, drift and signal quality against process context or a reference measurement [DOC-PRESSURE_TRANSMITTER-CORE].

practice_scenarios.title: Intermittent transmitter signal (fictional training case)
practice_scenarios.brief: Training transmitter TT-11 drops its signal for a few seconds several times a day, mostly after rain. Between dropouts the reading agrees with a reference gauge.

tasks.prompt: The reading is accurate between dropouts and worse after rain. Select the most likely component.
tasks.feedback_ok: Correct. Moisture getting past the gland to the terminals fits the pattern.
tasks.feedback_bad: The measurement itself is accurate, so the sensor is less likely. How could rain reach the wiring?

tasks.prompt: Why is sensor drift unlikely here?
options: The reading matches a reference between dropouts

tasks.prompt: What must be in place before opening a transmitter in the field?
options: Authorisation, hazardous-area rules, loop isolation and the approved procedure
Nothing if the signal is already lost

tasks.prompt: Virtual exercise: reach the terminals. Remove parts in a valid order.
tasks.feedback_ok: Terminals exposed in the virtual model.
tasks.feedback_bad: Not in this order. Free the cable entry first.

tasks.prompt: Reassemble the model (reverse order).

VIBRATION_SENSOR.label: Vibration sensor
VIBRATION_SENSOR.function: Converts machine vibration into an electrical signal; poor mounting or cabling makes the data unreliable.

components.name: Mounting stud
components.function: Threaded stud that couples the sensor rigidly to the machine.

components.name: Base
components.function: Flat base that must sit fully on a clean, flat machine surface.
failure_symptoms: Paint or dirt under the base

components.name: Piezo element
components.function: Ceramic crystal that produces charge when squeezed by the vibrating mass.

components.name: Seismic mass
components.function: Dense mass whose inertia squeezes the piezo element as the machine vibrates.

components.name: Housing
components.function: Sealed stainless case that protects the element and shields it electrically.

components.name: Connector
components.function: Top-exit connector for the signal cable.
failure_symptoms: Corroded or loose connector causing dropouts

components.name: Cable
components.function: Shielded cable to the monitoring system; routing and strain relief matter.

MOUNTING_ISSUE: Loose stud or poor mounting surface

steps.text: The sensor only measures what reaches it. A loose stud or a painted surface damps high frequencies and hides early bearing faults.
Inside, a mass squeezes a ceramic element as the machine moves. This part rarely fails, so check mounting and cabling first.
Dropouts and noise usually come from the connector or cable shield.
Poor sensor quality should lower confidence in every diagnosis that uses its data [DOC-VIBRATION_SENSOR-CORE].

practice_scenarios.title: Suspicious vibration reading (fictional training case)
practice_scenarios.brief: Training sensor TS-03 suddenly reads 40% lower than the sensor on the other side of the same bearing. Signal quality is normal.

tasks.prompt: Signal quality is fine but the level dropped suddenly. Select the most likely component.
tasks.feedback_ok: Correct. A sudden lower reading with a clean signal fits a loosened mounting.
tasks.feedback_bad: The signal is clean, so cabling is less likely. What couples the sensor to the machine?

tasks.prompt: Why compare with the sensor on the other side of the bearing?
options: It separates a sensor problem from a real change in the machine
It is closer to the control room

tasks.prompt: What must be in place before touching a sensor on a running machine?
options: Authorisation, a safe access assessment and the site procedure

tasks.prompt: Virtual exercise: reach the mounting stud. Remove parts in a valid order.
tasks.feedback_ok: Mounting exposed in the virtual model.
tasks.feedback_bad: Not in this order. Disconnect the cable first.

tasks.prompt: Reassemble the model (reverse order).
